subject: hardware-workshop
name: Hardware Workshop
exam: TU assessment: 60% final examination set by the university, 40% internal (assignments, lab work, attendance). Confirm the split in your college's notice.

units.title: Safety, Tools and the Components of a PC
topics: Inside the PC: components and what their specs mean
Eight rules of safe and careful workshop practice

sections.title: Inside the PC: components and what their specs mean
Eight rules of safe and careful workshop practice

summary: Protect yourself and the parts: unplug, discharge static, never open a PSU.
The toolkit is small and cheap; a multimeter, crimper and a bootable USB solve most jobs.
Every component has a few specifications that decide compatibility and performance.
Simple arithmetic selects the PSU, UPS and storage layout and explains real speeds and capacities.

units.title: Assembling a Desktop PC, Step by Step
topics: Eight common assembly mistakes and how to avoid them

sections.title: Eight common assembly mistakes and how to avoid them

summary: Build in a fixed order, handling the CPU and RAM carefully and tightening screws evenly.
Front-panel headers need the manual; LEDs have polarity, switches do not.
Check twice before power-on: no loose screws, all power connected, monitor on the right port.
If it fails, use beep codes, debug LEDs and a minimum-configuration test to isolate the part.

units.title: BIOS/UEFI, Disk Partitioning and Operating System Installation
topics: Eight tips for a safe operating-system installation

sections.title: Eight tips for a safe operating-system installation

summary: UEFI replaces BIOS and brings GPT, Secure Boot and speed; the settings to master are boot order, SATA mode, virtualisation and Secure Boot.
Partition tables and file systems have hard limits that explain real-world behaviour (2 TiB MBR, 4 GiB FAT32).
A clean install follows a fixed routine, and the work is not finished until drivers, updates and a backup are done.
Virtual machines and live USBs are the safest places to practise and repair.

units.title: Troubleshooting, Maintenance, Peripherals and Network Cabling
summary: Methodical troubleshooting beats guessing: simplest cause first, one change at a time, known-good parts.
Preventive maintenance (cleaning, updates, backups, UPS) avoids most failures.
Printers, monitors and input devices have well-known faults with simple remedies.
A good Ethernet cable follows one colour standard on both ends, and a tester proves it.
